# Blueprint 01: Enterprise Technical Support Automation

## 1. Executive Summary

This blueprint defines a production-grade, zero-trust **Enterprise Technical Support Automation** architecture on Google Cloud Platform (GCP). It automates Level-1 (L1) ticket triage and knowledge-grounded resolution while orchestrating deterministic Level-2 (L2) escalations into Zendesk and Jira through an **Agent Development Kit (ADK)** tool-calling agent.

Key architectural properties:
- **Zero Idle Cost Compute & Vector Storage**: All stateless API, retrieval, and agent services run on **Cloud Run v2** (`min_instance_count = 0` for pilot/off-peak; optional warm instances for enterprise P99 latency SLAs), paired with **Cloud Firestore Vector Search** ($0 idle baseline; see [ADR-002](../../adrs/ADR-002-firestore-vector-search-vs-vertex-ai-vector-search.md)).
- **Privacy-by-Design LLM Pipeline**: Every inbound ticket passes through **Cloud DLP (Sensitive Data Protection)** inline de-identification and **Model Armor** prompt-injection screening *before* any token reaches **Vertex AI**.
- **Tiered Cost-Optimized Inference**: 85% of routine L1 inquiries route to **Gemini 3.8 Flash**; only the top 15% high-complexity diagnostic or multi-system escalations escalate to **Gemini Pro** (see [ADR-003](../../adrs/ADR-003-gemini-flash-vs-pro-model-routing.md)).
- **Strict Network Egress Governance**: Outbound calls to Zendesk and Jira traverse **Direct VPC Egress** and **Cloud NAT** with static allowlisted IP addresses; all Google API calls stay on Google's private backbone via **Private Service Connect (PSC)** inside a **VPC Service Controls (VPC-SC)** perimeter.

---

## 2. Business SLA & Technical SLO Targets

| Metric | Target SLO | Measurement Window | Enforcement Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **API Availability** | 99.95% | Rolling 30 days | Multi-zone Cloud Run v2 + External ALB health checks |
| **L1 Grounded Resolution Latency (P95)** | <= 2.8 s | Rolling 7 days | Gemini 3.8 Flash streaming + Firestore composite vector index |
| **L2 Escalation Latency (P95)** | <= 6.5 s | Rolling 7 days | Gemini Pro + bounded 3-step ADK tool loop (5s timeout/tool) |
| **L1 Autonomous Deflection Rate** | >= 62% | Monthly | Confidence threshold >= 0.80 + citation grounding verification |
| **PII Leakage to LLM Rate** | 0.00% | Continuous | Mandatory synchronous Cloud DLP gate (fail-closed on DLP error) |
| **Grounded Citation Fidelity** | >= 96% | Weekly eval batch | Automated Vertex AI Eval / NLI entailment check in BigQuery |
| **Idle Infrastructure Cost** | $0.00 / mo | Pilot / Non-prod | Cloud Run `min_instances = 0` + Firestore serverless vector index |

---

## 4. Runtime Request & Security Sequence

> Source: [sequence-diagram.mmd](./sequence-diagram.mmd)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Enterprise Customer
    participant Edge as Cloud Armor + WIF/IAP Edge
    participant GW as Cloud Run Triage API
    participant DLP as Cloud DLP (via PSC)
    participant MA as Model Armor (via PSC)
    participant RAG as Vector RAG + Firestore
    participant ADK as ADK Triage & Escalation Agent
    participant LLM as Vertex AI (Flash / Pro)
    participant Ticketing as Zendesk / Jira (NAT + SWP)
    participant Audit as Cloud Logging + BigQuery

    User->>Edge: Submit support ticket (HTTPS + Tenant JWT / BFF OIDC)
    Edge->>Edge: Evaluate WAF rules, IP rate limits, verify JWT/HMAC
    Edge->>GW: Forward authenticated request (X-Tenant-ID, Request-ID)

    GW->>DLP: content.deidentify(ticket_text, InfoTypes: PII/PCI)
    DLP-->>GW: Redacted text + ephemeral surrogate map

    GW->>MA: sanitizeUserPrompt(redacted_text)
    alt Prompt Injection Detected
        MA-->>GW: BLOCK (Confidence >= 0.85)
        GW->>Audit: Log security event (OWASP LLM01)
        GW-->>User: 400 Safe fallback message
    else Prompt Safe
        MA-->>GW: ALLOW
        GW->>RAG: Retrieve top-8 KB chunks (tenant_id + product_tier filter)
        RAG->>RAG: Embed query (text-embedding-005) + Firestore find_nearest()
        RAG-->>GW: Ranked grounded chunks + citations

        GW->>MA: sanitizeModelInput(retrieved_chunks)
        MA-->>GW: ALLOW (Indirect injection check passed)

        GW->>ADK: Invoke ADK Agent (OIDC IAM, redacted_text, screened_chunks)
        ADK->>LLM: Route to Gemini 3.8 Flash (L1 85%) or Gemini Pro (L2 15%)
        LLM-->>ADK: Draft response + confidence score + tool_call (if escalation)

        alt Confidence >= 0.80 (L1 Deflection)
            ADK->>Audit: Emit latency, tokens, citations, deflection=true
            ADK-->>GW: Grounded answer with KB citations
            GW-->>User: Grounded answer with KB citations
        else Confidence < 0.80 or Escalation Tool Requested
            ADK->>Ticketing: Create/update Zendesk & Jira issue via Cloud NAT + SWP
            Ticketing-->>ADK: Ticket ID (ZD-48219 / SUP-1042)
            ADK->>Audit: Emit escalation telemetry + tool audit record
            ADK-->>GW: Escalation summary + Ticket ID
            GW-->>User: Ticket created (ZD-48219) with diagnostic summary
        end
    end
```

## 5. Failure Modes & Resilience Patterns

| Failure Scenario | Blast Radius | Automated Mitigation | Recovery SLO |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cloud DLP API timeout / 5xx** | Inbound triage halted | **Fail-closed** — never bypass DLP. Retry with exponential backoff (200ms, 500ms); after 2 retries, queue ticket to human Zendesk queue without LLM invocation. | < 2s fallback |
| **Vertex AI 429 Quota / Regional Degradation** | LLM synthesis degraded | Cross-region fallback (`us-central1` -> `us-east4`) with circuit breaker (open after 5 consecutive 5xx in 30s). | < 5s failover |
| **Firestore Vector Index Cold Latency** | Slight P95 spike | Pre-filter by `tenant_id` and `product_tier` composite index to restrict ANN search space to < 50k vectors per tenant. | P95 < 180ms |
| **Zendesk / Jira API Outage** | L2 escalation delayed | ADK escalation tool writes idempotent retry payload (`idempotency_key = sha256(ticket_id)`) to dead-letter Cloud Tasks queue with backoff up to 24h. | Zero ticket loss |
| **LLM Hallucination / Low Grounding** | Incorrect user guidance | Mandatory confidence threshold (`>= 0.80`) + strict citation regex check against retrieved Firestore document IDs; failing responses auto-escalate to L2. | 100% gated |

---

## 6. Observability & LLMOps KPIs

All Cloud Run services emit structured JSON logs to **Cloud Logging** with a BigQuery Log Sink (`llmops_support_events`) partitioned by `event_date` and clustered by `tenant_id`, `model_tier`:

- **Operational Metrics (Cloud Monitoring)**: Request rate, error rate (4xx/5xx), Cloud Run cold-start ratio, P50/P95/P99 latency per microservice, Cloud NAT port utilization.
- **LLMOps Metrics (BigQuery)**:
  - `deflection_rate = COUNTIF(escalated = FALSE) / COUNT(*)`
  - `cost_per_resolved_ticket = SUM(dlp_cost + embed_cost + llm_cost) / COUNTIF(escalated = FALSE)`
  - `pro_escalation_share` (target <= 15%; alerts if > 20% indicating prompt drift)
  - `model_armor_block_rate` (security anomaly alert if > 2% of tenant traffic)

  - [STRIDE & OWASP LLM Top 10 Threat Model](./security-threat-model.md)

  - [ADR-002: Firestore Vector Search vs Vertex AI Vector Search](../../adrs/ADR-002-firestore-vector-search-vs-vertex-ai-vector-search.md)
  - [ADR-003: Gemini Flash vs Pro Model Routing](../../adrs/ADR-003-gemini-flash-vs-pro-model-routing.md)

# Blueprint 01: Monthly GCP Cost Estimation — Technical Support Automation

## 1. Pricing Baseline & Workload Assumptions

All unit prices reflect standard `us-central1` on-demand GCP list pricing (no Committed Use Discounts assumed; 1-year/3-year CUDs reduce Vertex AI and Cloud Run compute by 20%–37%).

### Per-Request Workload Profile
- **Average Inbound Ticket + Context Payload**: 4 KB raw text inspected by **Cloud DLP** (0.000004 GB/req).
- **Average Query Embedding**: 150 input tokens via **Vertex AI `text-embedding-005`** ($0.025 / 1M tokens).
- **Average Grounded RAG Prompt (8 chunks + system prompt + ticket)**: 2,400 input tokens; 450 output tokens.
- **Model Routing Split** (per [ADR-003](../../adrs/ADR-003-gemini-flash-vs-pro-model-routing.md); pre-routed via lightweight complexity/intent score):
  - **85% L1 Traffic -> Vertex AI Gemini 3.8 Flash**: $0.15 / 1M input tokens, $0.60 / 1M output tokens.
  - **15% L2 Traffic -> Vertex AI Gemini Pro**: $1.25 / 1M input tokens, $5.00 / 1M output tokens.
- **Cloud Run v2 Compute**: 3 services (`sa-support-gw`, `sa-rag-reader`, `sa-support-agent`), 1 vCPU / 1 GiB RAM, avg 1.2 s combined active CPU-time per request ($0.00002400/vCPU-sec, $0.00000250/GiB-sec, $0.40/1M requests).
  - **Pilot (10k req/mo)** & **Growth (100k req/mo)**: `min_instance_count = 0` (**Zero Idle Cost**).
  - **Enterprise (1M req/mo)**: `min_instance_count = 1` on `sa-support-gw` and `sa-rag-reader` (2 warm instances total at $12.88/mo each = **+$25.76/mo** idle baseline) to guarantee P99 < 2.8 s without cold starts.
- **Cloud Firestore Vector Search**: 8 document reads per request ($0.06 / 100k reads) + 1 audit write per 5 requests ($0.18 / 100k writes) + 2 GB / 10 GB / 50 GB vector+doc storage ($0.18/GB-mo). **$0 idle index hosting fee.**
  - Pilot: `(80k*$0.06/100k) + (2k*$0.18/100k) + (2*$0.18) = $0.05 + $0.00 + $0.36 = $0.41`
  - Growth: `(800k*$0.06/100k) + (20k*$0.18/100k) + (10*$0.18) = $0.48 + $0.04 + $1.80 = $2.32`
  - Enterprise: `(8M*$0.06/100k) + (200k*$0.18/100k) + (50*$0.18) = $4.80 + $0.36 + $9.00 = $14.16`
- **Cloud DLP (Sensitive Data Protection)**: $1.00 / GB inspected + $2.00 / GB de-identified = $3.00 / GB combined.
- **Model Armor**: 2 screening calls per request (user prompt + retrieved RAG chunks) modeled at $0.10 / 1,000 requests screened ($0.20 / 1,000 tickets).
- **Networking & Security**: External ALB forwarding rule ($18.25/mo) + Cloud Armor policy & rules ($6.00/mo + $0.75/1M req) + Cloud NAT gateway ($32.85/mo + $0.045/GB) + Private Service Connect endpoint ($7.30/mo). (Dedicated single-workload networking is shown transparently; Shared VPC amortization removes the $64.40/mo fixed base.)
- **Secret Manager + Cloud KMS (CMEK)**: 3 active secrets ($0.18/mo) + 2 CMEK keys ($2.00/mo) + API access operations.
- **Cloud Logging + Monitoring + BigQuery**: Structured audit sink + weekly LLMOps eval queries.

---

## 2. Monthly Cost Comparison Across 3 Enterprise Traffic Tiers

| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| **Cloud Run v2** (Triage GW + RAG + ADK) | $0.35 | $3.54 | $61.16 | Active compute (`min=0` Pilot/Growth) + 2 warm instances in Enterprise ($25.76) |
| **Vertex AI — Gemini 3.8 Flash** (85% L1) | $5.36 | $53.55 | $535.50 | `0.85 * N * (2400*0.15 + 450*0.60) / 1e6` |
| **Vertex AI — Gemini Pro** (15% L2) | $7.88 | $78.75 | $787.50 | `0.15 * N * (2400*1.25 + 450*5.00) / 1e6` |
| **Vertex AI — text-embedding-005** | $0.04 | $0.38 | $3.75 | `N * 150 tokens * $0.025 / 1e6` |
| **Cloud Firestore (Native + Vector Search)** | $0.41 | $2.32 | $14.16 | `8 reads/req` ($0.06/100k) + `0.2 writes/req` + storage (2/10/50 GB * $0.18) |
| **Cloud DLP (Inspect + De-identify)** | $0.12 | $1.20 | $12.00 | `N * 4 KB = 0.04 / 0.4 / 4.0 GB * $3.00/GB` |
| **Model Armor (Prompt + RAG Screening)** | $2.00 | $20.00 | $200.00 | `2 * N * $0.10 / 1,000 screening calls` |
| **External ALB + Cloud Armor + IAP** | $24.26 | $24.33 | $25.00 | Base LB ($18.25) + Armor policy ($6.00) + $0.75/1M req |
| **Cloud NAT + Private Service Connect** | $40.15 | $40.17 | $40.35 | NAT gateway ($32.85) + PSC endpoint ($7.30) + egress GB |
| **Secret Manager + Cloud KMS (CMEK)** | $2.18 | $2.21 | $2.50 | 2 CMEK keys ($2.00) + 3 secrets ($0.18) + access ops |
| **Cloud Logging + Monitoring + BigQuery** | $1.50 | $4.50 | $24.00 | Ingestion + BQ storage + weekly LLMOps eval queries |
| **Total Estimated Monthly Cost** | **$84.25** | **$230.95** | **$1,705.92** | **Exact sum of all line items above** |
| **Effective Cost per Support Ticket** | **$0.0084** | **$0.0023** | **$0.0017** | Total Monthly Cost / Monthly Requests |

---

## 3. Unit Economics & FinOps Sensitivity

1. **Human Support Cost Comparison**: At an enterprise average of $14.00 per L1 human-handled support ticket and a conservative 62% autonomous deflection rate, **100,000 tickets/month** yields 62,000 deflected tickets = **$868,000/mo gross labor avoidance** against **$230.95/mo** GCP runtime cost.
2. **Why Firestore Vector Search Dominates at Pilot, Growth & Enterprise**: Replacing Firestore Vector Search ($0.41/mo Pilot, $2.32/mo Growth, $14.16/mo Enterprise) with a dedicated **Vertex AI Vector Search** HA index endpoint (~$260/mo always-on baseline) would inflate Pilot infrastructure spend by **+308%** for zero latency benefit under 10M chunks.
3. **Model Routing Lever**: Without Flash/Pro routing (sending 100% of Enterprise 1M req/mo to Gemini Pro), LLM spend jumps from **$1,323.00/mo** to **$5,250.00/mo** (+$3,927/mo, a **3.97x** increase).
4. **Shared VPC Amortization**: Organizations deploying this blueprint onto an existing Enterprise Shared VPC with centralized ALB + Cloud NAT amortize the $64.40/mo networking base across workloads, dropping Pilot marginal cost to **$19.85/mo**.

# Blueprint 01: Security Threat Model (STRIDE & OWASP LLM Top 10) ## 1. Security Boundaries & Trust Zones 1. **Zone 0 (Untrusted Internet)**: Web widget, Slack webhooks, email gateways, Zendesk/Jira SaaS endpoints. 2. **Zone 1 (GCP Edge Perimeter)**: External Application Load Balancer (TLS 1.3), Cloud Armor WAF, Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) / OIDC JWT verifier. 3. **Zone 2 (VPC-SC Protected Compute)**: Private Cloud Run v2 services (`sa-support-gw`, `sa-rag-reader`, `sa-support-agent`) with `ingress = internal-and-cloud-load-balancing` (GW) and `ingress = internal` (RAG & ADK). 4. **Zone 3 (Managed AI & Data Plane)**: Cloud DLP, Model Armor, Cloud Firestore Vector Search, Vertex AI, Secret Manager, Cloud KMS (CMEK), BigQuery audit sink — accessed exclusively over **Private Service Connect (PSC)**. --- ## 2. # Blueprint 02: Enterprise Contract Processing & Risk Extraction Pipeline

## 1. Executive Summary

This blueprint defines a fully asynchronous, event-driven **Enterprise Contract Processing & Risk Extraction Pipeline** on GCP for legal, procurement, and compliance teams. It ingests multi-page counterparty PDFs (MSAs, DPAs, SOWs, NDAs), extracts structured clause hierarchies via **Document AI**, applies **Cloud DLP deterministic format-preserving tokenization** to protect PII and financial identifiers, and performs tiered legal risk analysis using **Gemini 3.8 Flash** and **Gemini Pro** inside a **VPC Service Controls (VPC-SC)** perimeter.

Key architectural properties:
- **Zero Idle Cost Event-Driven Execution**: **Cloud Storage + Eventarc + Cloud Workflows + Cloud Run Jobs** scale strictly to zero between contract batches — zero always-on VMs, zero idle GKE nodes, zero polling daemons.
- **Deterministic Tokenization Over Destructive Masking**: Using **Cloud DLP `CRYPTO_DETERMINISTIC`** wrapped with a **Cloud KMS (CMEK)** key preserves entity coreference (e.g., `[PARTY_A_9f2a]` remains consistent across 40 pages so Gemini Pro can accurately analyze obligations) without exposing real names, tax IDs, or bank accounts to the LLM (see [ADR-004](../../adrs/ADR-004-cloud-dlp-sensitive-data-anonymization.md)).
- **Tiered Legal Inference Routing**: 75% of contract clauses (dates, renewal windows, payment terms, governing law) are extracted by **Gemini 3.8 Flash**; only the 25% legally dense clauses (indemnification, limitation of liability, IP assignment, change of control) escalate to **Gemini Pro** (see [ADR-003](../../adrs/ADR-003-gemini-flash-vs-pro-model-routing.md)).
- **Immutable Compliance Lineage**: Every extraction writes an append-only audit record into **BigQuery** containing contract SHA-256, Document AI page bounding boxes, DLP finding counts, model version IDs, and clause-level risk rationales.

---

## 2. Business SLA & Technical SLO Targets

| Metric | Target SLO | Measurement Window | Enforcement Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **End-to-End Processing Latency (20-page PDF, P95)** | <= 45 s | Rolling 30 days | Parallel Document AI layout + concurrent Cloud Run Job clause batches |
| **Pipeline Delivery Durability** | 99.99% (Zero lost PDFs) | Rolling 90 days | GCS Object Versioning + Cloud Workflows durable retries + DLQ |
| **High-Risk Clause Recall (Indemnity / Liability)** | >= 98.5% | Monthly legal QA | Gemini Pro rubric extraction + mandatory negative-clause verification |
| **PII / Financial ID Exposure to LLM** | 0.00% | Continuous | Mandatory Cloud Workflows DLP gate before Cloud Run Job dispatch |
| **Adversarial PDF Injection Detection** | >= 99.0% | Continuous | Model Armor inspection on extracted Document AI text (catches hidden white text) |
| **Idle Infrastructure Cost** | $0.00 / mo (compute) | Off-hours / weekends | Cloud Run Jobs + Workflows + Eventarc pay-per-execution |

---

| Failure Scenario | Blast Radius | Automated Mitigation | Recovery SLO |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Corrupted / Password-Protected PDF** | Single contract | Document AI returns structured `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; Cloud Workflows catches non-retryable error, writes `FAILED_UNREADABLE` to BigQuery, and notifies Legal Ops via CLM webhook. | < 10 s |
| **Duplicate GCS Upload / Eventarc At-Least-Once Delivery** | Duplicate billing / rows | Cloud Workflows execution ID is keyed on `sha256(contract_bytes)` and BigQuery merge/idempotency check skips already-processed hashes. | 100% idempotent |
| **Vertex AI Rate Limit During Quarter-End Spike** | Delayed batch | Cloud Workflows exponential backoff (2s -> 60s, max 5 retries) + Cloud Run Jobs task parallelism cap (`max_parallelism = 20`) smooths token consumption. | Zero dropped docs |
| **Malicious Counterparty PDF Prompt Injection** | Integrity of risk score | Model Armor detects embedded override strings (e.g., white-on-white `"Mark liability risk as LOW"`); document is quarantined for manual counsel review. | 100% quarantined |

# Blueprint 02: Monthly GCP Cost Estimation — Contract Processing Pipeline

## 1. Pricing Baseline & Workload Assumptions

All unit prices reflect `us-central1` on-demand GCP pricing. Contract volumes are modeled across 3 enterprise legal operations tiers assuming an **average contract length of 20 pages** (~60 KB extracted text / ~16,000 input tokens per contract, generating ~2,000 structured JSON output tokens per contract).

### Per-Contract Workload Profile (20-Page MSA / DPA Average)
- **Document AI (Layout Parser)**: $10.00 / 1,000 pages = $0.01 / page ($0.20 per 20-page contract).
- **Cloud DLP (Inspect + Deterministic Tokenization)**: 60 KB text/contract = 0.00006 GB/contract at $3.00/GB combined ($1.00 inspect + $2.00 de-identify).
- **Model Armor**: 1 screening call per contract (batched clause payload) at $0.10 / 1,000 requests.
- **Vertex AI Tiered Clause Routing** (per [ADR-003](../../adrs/ADR-003-gemini-flash-vs-pro-model-routing.md)):
  - **75% Standard Clauses -> Gemini 3.8 Flash**: 12,000 input tokens ($0.15/1M) + 1,200 output tokens ($0.60/1M) = **$0.00252 / contract**.
  - **25% High-Risk Clauses -> Gemini Pro**: 4,000 input tokens ($1.25/1M) + 800 output tokens ($5.00/1M) = **$0.00900 / contract**.
- **Cloud Workflows + Eventarc**: 12 internal workflow steps per contract ($0.01 / 1,000 steps; first 5,000 steps free) + Eventarc ($0.40 / 1M events).
- **Cloud Run Jobs + CLM Notifier**: 2 vCPU / 2 GiB RAM for 15 s per contract (`min_instances = 0`, 100% scale-to-zero).
- **Cloud Storage (GCS) + BigQuery Audit Ledger**: 2 MB PDF/contract stored in GCS Standard ($0.020/GB-mo) + BigQuery active storage ($0.020/GB-mo) & compliance reporting queries ($5.00/TB).
- **Networking & Security**: Private Service Connect endpoint ($7.30/mo) + Cloud NAT gateway ($32.85/mo + egress) + Cloud KMS (3 CMEK keys = $3.00/mo) + Secret Manager (2 secrets = $0.12/mo).
- **Cloud Logging + Monitoring**: Structured pipeline audit logs & SLA dashboards.

---

# Blueprint 03: Internal Enterprise Agent Connected to SQL Databases

## 1. Executive Summary

This blueprint defines a zero-trust, read-only **Internal Enterprise SQL Analytics Agent** on GCP that lets finance, operations, and BI teams query **Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL** and **BigQuery** in natural language — without ever exposing raw database credentials, risking destructive DDL/DML execution, leaking cross-department rows, or triggering runaway BigQuery scan bills.

Key architectural properties:
- **Standardized MCP Read-Only Tool Server**: Database access is strictly isolated inside a dedicated **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** server running on private **Cloud Run v2** (`sa-mcp-sql-ro`; see [ADR-006](../../adrs/ADR-006-mcp-and-a2a-enterprise-agent-interoperability.md)). The ADK agent has **zero direct network or IAM path** to Cloud SQL or BigQuery.
- **Deterministic SQL AST Guardrails (Zero LLM Trust)**: Every LLM-generated query is parsed into an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) before touching any database. Anything other than a single `SELECT` / `WITH ... SELECT` against allowlisted semantic views is hard-blocked; `LIMIT 500` and `statement_timeout = 8s` are injected deterministically.
- **Identity Propagation & Row-Level Security (RLS)**: Verified **Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)** user claims (`email`, `department`) are propagated into PostgreSQL `SET LOCAL app.user_dept` inside a `BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY` block and into BigQuery Row Access Policies — eliminating confused-deputy data leaks.
- **Query Cost Dry-Run Gate & Output PII Scrubbing**: BigQuery queries execute `dryRun = true` first and reject any scan > 10 GB; outbound SQL rows pass through **Cloud DLP** to scrub unexpected PII embedded in free-text note columns before reaching Vertex AI synthesis.

---

## 2. Business SLA & Technical SLO Targets

| Metric | Target SLO | Measurement Window | Enforcement Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Analytics Agent Availability** | 99.90% (Business Hours) | Rolling 30 days | Cloud Run v2 + Cloud SQL HA Read Replica + BigQuery |
| **End-to-End Query Latency (P95)** | <= 5.5 s | Rolling 7 days | Gemini 3.8 Flash (70% queries) + 8s SQL statement timeout |
| **Destructive SQL Execution Rate (DDL/DML)** | 0.00% (Hard Zero) | Continuous | Triple barrier: SQL AST parser + `READ ONLY` tx + DB read-only role |
| **Cross-Department RLS Leakage** | 0.00% (Hard Zero) | Continuous | IAP JWT propagation + DB-native RLS & BigQuery Row Access Policies |
| **Max Single-Query BigQuery Scan** | <= 10 GB ($0.05 cap) | Per query | Mandatory BigQuery `dryRun = true` gate in MCP server |
| **SQL Execution Accuracy (Valid & Correct)** | >= 93% | Bi-weekly golden set | Semantic catalog grounding + 1 automated syntax self-correction retry |

---

## 5. Failure Modes & Resilience Patterns

| Failure Scenario | Blast Radius | Automated Mitigation | Recovery SLO |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **LLM Generates Invalid SQL Syntax** | Single analyst query | MCP server returns structured PostgreSQL/BigQuery parse error; ADK agent executes max **1 bounded self-correction retry** before returning helpful clarification prompt. | < 3 s retry |
| **Expensive Full-Table BigQuery Scan** | FinOps budget | Mandatory `dryRun = true` check rejects any query > 10 GB before execution and advises analyst to add a partition date filter (`WHERE event_date >= ...`). | 0 bytes billed |
| **Cloud SQL Read Replica CPU Saturation** | Slow operational queries | Connection pool cap (`max_connections = 20` per Cloud Run instance) + `statement_timeout = 8000ms` + automatic fallback notice directing heavy historical queries to BigQuery. | Primary DB 100% isolated |
| **Unstructured Column Contains Unexpected PII** | Data governance | Synchronous **Cloud DLP** scans serialized SQL result rows before returning them to ADK or rendering to the analyst. | 100% scrubbed |

---

# Blueprint 03: Monthly GCP Cost Estimation — Internal SQL Analytics Agent

## 1. Pricing Baseline & Workload Assumptions

All unit prices reflect `us-central1` on-demand GCP pricing. Traffic tiers represent internal enterprise analytics usage (BI, Finance, RevOps, Executive Self-Service).

### Per-Query Workload Profile
- **Average LLM Token Budget (Schema Context + SQL Generation + Narrative Synthesis)**: 3,500 input tokens, 600 output tokens per analytical question.
- **Model Routing Split** (per [ADR-003](../../adrs/ADR-003-gemini-flash-vs-pro-model-routing.md)):
  - **70% Standard KPI / Aggregation Queries -> Vertex AI Gemini 3.8 Flash**: $0.15/1M input, $0.60/1M output.
  - **30% Complex Multi-CTE / Window Function Queries -> Vertex AI Gemini Pro**: $1.25/1M input, $5.00/1M output.
- **Cloud Run v2 Compute** (`sa-sql-agent` + `sa-mcp-sql-ro`): 1 vCPU / 1 GiB RAM, avg 1.5 s active CPU-time per query (`min_instances = 0` for Pilot & Growth; 1 warm MCP instance in Enterprise = **+$12.88/mo**).
- **Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL (Read Replica)**:
  - Note: Most enterprises connect to an **existing** Cloud SQL primary by adding a dedicated **read-only replica** so AI queries never contend with OLTP production. Dedicated replica sizing shown transparently:
    - Pilot: `db-custom-1-3840` (1 vCPU, 3.75 GB RAM, 50 GB SSD, Private IP) = **$59.50/mo**.
    - Growth: `db-custom-2-7680` (2 vCPU, 7.5 GB RAM, 100 GB SSD) = **$119.00/mo**.
    - Enterprise: `db-custom-4-15360` (4 vCPU, 15 GB RAM, 250 GB SSD) = **$248.00/mo**.
- **BigQuery Analytical Queries**: Avg 250 MB scanned per query (enforced via partition pruning + 10 GB dry-run cap) at $5.00/TB ($0.00125/query) after 1 TB/mo free tier.
- **Cloud DLP (Input + Output Row Scrubbing)**: Avg 20 KB SQL result table + prompt per query at $3.00/GB combined.
- **Model Armor**: $0.10 / 1,000 queries screened.
- **Networking & Security**: Application Load Balancer ($18.25/mo) + Cloud Armor ($6.00/mo) + Private Service Connect endpoint ($7.30/mo) + Cloud KMS (2 CMEK keys = $2.00/mo) + Secret Manager (2 secrets = $0.12/mo). (IAP is free on GCP.)
- **Cloud Audit Logs + Cloud Logging**: Immutable SQL query audit trail & cost ledger.

---

## 2. Monthly Cost Comparison Across 3 Enterprise Analytics Tiers

| GCP Service / Line Item | Pilot / Finance Team (5,000 queries/mo) | Growth / Multi-Dept BI (50,000 queries/mo) | Enterprise / Global Org (250,000 queries/mo) | Calculation Formula / Notes |

| **Cloud Run v2** (ADK Agent + MCP Server) | $0.22 | $2.22 | $23.98 | Active compute (`min=0` Pilot/Growth) + 1 warm MCP instance in Enterprise ($12.88) |

| **Vertex AI — Gemini Pro** (30% Complex SQL) | $11.06 | $110.63 | $553.13 | `0.30 * N * (3500*1.25 + 600*5.00) / 1e6` |
| **Cloud SQL PostgreSQL (Dedicated RO Replica)** | $59.50 | $119.00 | $248.00 | Private IP read replica (`1/2/4 vCPU`) isolating OLTP primary |
| **BigQuery (On-Demand Scans w/ 10GB Cap)** | $1.25 | $57.50 | $307.50 | `(N * 250 MB - 1 TB free tier) * $5.00/TB` (min $1.25 storage) |
| **Cloud DLP (Prompt + SQL Row Scrubbing)** | $0.30 | $3.00 | $15.00 | `N * 20 KB * $3.00/GB` |
| **Model Armor (Prompt Screening)** | $0.50 | $5.00 | $25.00 | `N * $0.10 / 1,000 queries` |
| **ALB + Cloud Armor + IAP + PSC** | $31.55 | $31.59 | $31.74 | ALB ($18.25) + Armor ($6.00) + PSC ($7.30) + IAP ($0.00) |
| **Cloud KMS (CMEK) + Secret Manager** | $2.12 | $2.15 | $2.30 | 2 CMEK keys ($2.00) + 2 secrets ($0.12) + ops |
| **Cloud Audit Logs + Cloud Logging** | $1.50 | $4.50 | $16.00 | Immutable SQL execution & identity audit trail |
| **Total Estimated Monthly Cost** | **$111.10** | **$366.57** | **$1,377.53** | **Exact sum of all line items above** |
| **Effective Cost per Analytics Query** | **$0.0222** | **$0.0073** | **$0.0055** | Total Monthly Cost / Monthly Queries |

---

## 3. FinOps Insights & Optimization Levers

1. **BigQuery-Only Zero-Idle Variant**: If the organization only queries BigQuery (no Cloud SQL PostgreSQL read replica required), removing the dedicated Cloud SQL replica drops Pilot monthly cost from **$111.10** to **$51.60/mo** (or **$20.05/mo** on an existing Shared VPC ALB).
2. **Dry-Run Guardrail ROI**: A single unpartitioned `SELECT *` against a 50 TB enterprise BigQuery event table costs **$250.00**. The MCP server's mandatory 10 GB dry-run cap ($0.05 max per query) pays for the entire Cloud Run + DLP + Model Armor stack in a single prevented mistake.
3. **Semantic Caching**: Caching frequent recurring executive KPIs (e.g., daily revenue rollups) in BigQuery BI Engine or a 5-minute TTL response cache cuts Growth/Enterprise LLM + BigQuery scan costs by 25%–40%.

adrs.content:
# ADR-001: Cloud Run v2 (`min_instances=0`) over GKE Autopilot/Standard

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Date**: 2026-11-23
- **Applies To**: Blueprint 01 (Support Automation), Blueprint 02 (Contract Processing Jobs), Blueprint 03 (SQL Analytics Agent & MCP Server)

## Context

Enterprise AI agent orchestrators, RAG retrieval APIs, MCP tool servers, and asynchronous contract-extraction workers are **I/O-bound, stateless, and bursty** (spending 85%–95% of wall-clock request time awaiting Vertex AI, Document AI, Cloud DLP, or database responses). Teams frequently default to Kubernetes (GKE Standard or Autopilot) out of organizational habit, incurring permanent cluster management fees, node idle overhead, and platform engineering burden.

## Decision Drivers

1. **Zero Idle Cost Policy**: Pilot, staging, and off-hours enterprise workloads must incur **$0.00/mo** in idle compute.
2. **Fast Horizontal Bursting**: Quarter-end contract spikes (Blueprint 02) and support incident surges (Blueprint 01) require sub-5-second scale-out without node provisioning delays.
3. **Enterprise Network Security**: Must support Direct VPC Egress, Private Service Connect (PSC), VPC Service Controls, and per-service IAM Workload Identity without managing CNI plugins or Istio meshes.
4. **Operational Simplicity**: Minimize Kubernetes upgrade toil, kube-proxy tuning, and pod disruption budget maintenance for small-to-medium AI platform teams.

## Considered Options

1. **Option A: Cloud Run v2 Services & Jobs (`min_instance_count = 0` default; selective `min = 1` at Enterprise P99 tier)**
2. **Option B: GKE Autopilot (Regional Cluster)**
3. **Option C: GKE Standard (Self-Managed Node Pools)**

## Decision Outcome

**Chosen Option: Option A — Cloud Run v2 Services & Jobs.**

All stateless AI APIs, ADK agents, MCP tool servers, and batch contract extractors run on Cloud Run v2 with `min_instance_count = 0` for Pilot/Growth tiers and targeted `min_instance_count = 1` only on latency-critical customer-facing services at Enterprise scale (1M+ req/mo).

## Quantitative Trade-off Matrix

| Criterion | Cloud Run v2 (`min=0`) | GKE Autopilot (Regional) | GKE Standard (3x e2-standard-4) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cluster Management Fee** | $0.00 / mo | $74.40 / mo (after 1st free tier) | $74.40 / mo |
| **Idle Baseline Cost (Off-Peak)** | **$0.00 / mo** | ~$95–$160 / mo (system pods + min replicas) | ~$295 / mo (3 always-on nodes) |
| **Growth Tier Compute (BP01, 100k req/mo)** | **$3.54 / mo** | ~$145 / mo | ~$369 / mo |
| **Scale-Out Latency (0 -> 20 instances)** | **1.5 – 3.5 s** | 45 – 90 s (node auto-provisioning) | 40 – 75 s (cluster autoscaler) |
| **Cold Start Penalty (`min=0`)** | 400 – 900 ms (mitigated via `min=1` = $12.88/mo) | 0 ms (always-on pods) | 0 ms (always-on pods) |
| **GPU / Custom DaemonSet Support** | L4 GPU supported (no DaemonSets) | Full K8s ecosystem | Full K8s + custom kernel/GPU |
| **Operational Overhead (SRE hrs/mo)** | **< 2 hrs/mo** | 8 – 15 hrs/mo | 20 – 40 hrs/mo |

## Consequences

- **Positive**: 95%+ compute cost reduction at Pilot and Growth tiers; native OIDC IAM service-to-service auth (`roles/run.invoker`); Direct VPC Egress without managing VPC connectors; native Cloud Run Jobs for Blueprint 02 batch extraction.
- **Negative**: Request timeout capped at 60 minutes (irrelevant for interactive agents; batch jobs support 24h); no sidecar DaemonSets or custom Kubernetes CRDs.

## Revisit Triggers

Migrate a specific workload from Cloud Run v2 to **GKE Autopilot/Standard** ONLY when one or more of the following thresholds is crossed:
1. **Sustained High Utilization**: Workload sustains > 40% average CPU across **> 30 vCPUs 24/7** where GKE Committed Use Discounts + bin-packing beat Cloud Run per-second billing by > 25%.
2. **Self-Hosted Open-Weight GPUs**: Requirement to run multi-node vLLM / H100/A100 inference clusters (e.g., Llama / Gemma fine-tunes) with custom NCCL networking.
3. **Stateful Mesh / Protocol Requirements**: Requirement for persistent gRPC bidirectional long-lived stateful streams, custom eBPF/Cilium network policies, or complex Kubernetes Operators.

Many teams instinctively provision **Vertex AI Vector Search (Matching Engine)** Index Endpoints or third-party managed vector databases (Pinecone/Qdrant), unaware that Vertex AI Vector Search requires dedicated 24/7 deployed index nodes costing $150–$220+/month even at **zero queries**.
adrs.decisionOutcome: **Chosen Option: Option A — Cloud Firestore Vector Search.**
adrs.content:
# ADR-002: Cloud Firestore Vector Search over Vertex AI Vector Search Index Endpoints

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Date**: 2026-11-23
- **Applies To**: Blueprint 01 (Technical Support Automation Hybrid RAG)

## Context

Blueprint 01 requires a multi-tenant Knowledge Base (KB) capable of semantic retrieval over 768-dimensional `text-embedding-005` vectors combined with **strict pre-filtered metadata predicates** (`tenant_id == X`, `product_tier == Y`, `doc_status == "published"`). Many teams instinctively provision **Vertex AI Vector Search (Matching Engine)** Index Endpoints or third-party managed vector databases (Pinecone/Qdrant), unaware that Vertex AI Vector Search requires dedicated 24/7 deployed index nodes costing $150–$220+/month even at **zero queries**.

## Decision Drivers

1. **Zero Idle Cost Policy**: Vector storage and indexing must cost **$0.00/mo** when idle during pilot/staging and scale purely with read volume.
2. **Strict Multi-Tenant Isolation**: Metadata filtering (`tenant_id`) must execute **natively inside the database index** (not post-filtering in application RAM) to guarantee zero cross-tenant leakage.
3. **Native GCP Security & Simplicity**: Must live inside the GCP VPC-SC perimeter, support CMEK encryption, and avoid cross-cloud data egress or third-party vendor procurement.
4. **Operational Cohesion**: Document metadata, full chunk text, citations, and vector embeddings should live in one strongly consistent store (eliminating dual-write sync drift between a vector DB and a document DB).

## Considered Options

1. **Option A: Cloud Firestore (Native Mode) with Vector Search (`find_nearest` + Composite Indexes)**
2. **Option B: Vertex AI Vector Search (Matching Engine Index Endpoint)**
3. **Option C: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL + `pgvector` (HNSW)**

## Decision Outcome

**Chosen Option: Option A — Cloud Firestore Vector Search.**

Firestore stores each KB chunk document alongside its 768-dim `VectorValue` field and tenant metadata, using composite vector indexes (`tenant_id ASC`, `product_tier ASC`, `embedding VECTOR<768>`) to execute single-hop filtered KNN/ANN retrieval inside the GCP VPC-SC perimeter at **$0 idle cost**.

## Quantitative Trade-off Matrix

| Criterion | Cloud Firestore Vector Search | Vertex AI Vector Search (e2-standard-2) | Cloud SQL + `pgvector` (2 vCPU) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Idle Monthly Cost (0 req/mo)** | **$0.00 / mo** (+ $0.18/GB storage) | **~$156 – $220 / mo** (24/7 deployed node) | **~$119 / mo** (24/7 DB instance) |
| **Pilot Tier (10k req/mo, 2 GB)** | **$0.41 / mo** | ~$165 / mo | ~$119 / mo |
| **Growth Tier (100k req/mo, 10 GB)** | **$2.32 / mo** | ~$185 / mo | ~$125 / mo |
| **Enterprise Tier (1M req/mo, 50 GB)** | **$14.16 / mo** | ~$280 / mo (2 HA replicas) | ~$260 / mo (HA + read replica) |
| **Break-Even Volume vs Vertex AI** | Cheaper up to **~52M 8-chunk queries/mo** (pure read cost) | Cheaper above **> 50M queries/mo** or > 10M vectors | Cheaper if existing DB reused |
| **P95 Query Latency (< 5M vectors)** | **45 – 140 ms** | 10 – 25 ms | 25 – 80 ms |
| **Single-Store Consistency (No Dual-Write)** | **Yes** (text + metadata + vector atomic) | No (requires separate doc store) | Yes |
| **Max Scale Ceiling** | ~10M vectors per collection (sweet spot) | **100M – 1B+ vectors** (ScaNN) | ~5M–20M vectors (RAM bound) |

### Break-Even Math
- Firestore read cost (8 retrieved chunks per RAG query): `8 docs/query * $0.06 / 100,000 reads = $0.0000048 / query` (**$4.80 per 1M 8-chunk RAG queries**).
- Vertex AI Vector Search minimum HA deployment (2x `e2-standard-2` replicas for 99.95% SLA): `~$260/mo` fixed baseline.
- At 50 GB storage ($9/mo in Firestore), Firestore remains strictly cheaper than Vertex AI Vector Search up to:
  `($260 - $9) / $4.80 per 1M queries ≈ 52.3M 8-chunk RAG queries/month` (before even factoring in the secondary document store required by Vertex AI Vector Search). Consequently, the real migration trigger to Vertex AI Vector Search is **corpus size (> 10M vectors in one namespace) or P99 latency (< 20 ms SLA)**, not query volume cost.

## Consequences

- **Positive**: Eliminates $156–$260/mo always-on vector endpoint tax; eliminates dual-write synchronization bugs; enforces atomic `tenant_id` pre-filtering; supports CMEK and VPC-SC natively.
- **Negative**: Higher latency than Vertex AI ScaNN at ultra-high QPS (> 500 QPS) or > 10M vectors per unpartitioned collection; cosine/dot-product/Euclidean only (no custom hybrid BM25 without a secondary keyword token array).

## Revisit Triggers

Migrate to **Vertex AI Vector Search** ONLY when:
1. Corpus exceeds **10,000,000 vectors** in a single searchable namespace without natural tenant partitioning, OR
2. Sustained retrieval load exceeds **5,000,000 RAG queries/month** (~2+ sustained QPS 24/7) AND P99 vector retrieval latency must be strictly **< 20 ms**.

adrs.title: ADR-003: Per-Node Model Routing — Gemini 3.8 Flash vs Gemini Pro
adrs.summary: Routing 100% of enterprise AI traffic to a frontier reasoning model (**Gemini Pro**) destroys unit economics and inflates P95 latency, whereas routing 100% of traffic to a fast distilled model (**Gemini 3.8 Flash**) degrades accuracy on legally dense contract clauses (indemnification, limitation of liability) and complex multi-CTE SQL window functions.
adrs.decisionOutcome: **Chosen Option: Option A — Tiered Per-Node Model Routing.**
adrs.content:
# ADR-003: Per-Node Model Routing — Gemini 3.8 Flash vs Gemini Pro

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Date**: 2026-11-23
- **Applies To**: Blueprint 01 (Support), Blueprint 02 (Contracts), Blueprint 03 (SQL Analytics)

## Context

Routing 100% of enterprise AI traffic to a frontier reasoning model (**Gemini Pro**) destroys unit economics and inflates P95 latency, whereas routing 100% of traffic to a fast distilled model (**Gemini 3.8 Flash**) degrades accuracy on legally dense contract clauses (indemnification, limitation of liability) and complex multi-CTE SQL window functions.

## Decision Drivers

1. **FinOps Efficiency**: Reduce LLM token spend by **60%–75%** without sacrificing accuracy on high-risk reasoning nodes.
2. **Latency SLOs**: Meet P95 <= 2.8 s for L1 technical support (Blueprint 01) and P95 <= 5.5 s for interactive SQL analytics (Blueprint 03).
3. **Deterministic Escalation**: Routing decisions must be auditable, observable in BigQuery, and tunable via thresholds without code redeployments.

## Considered Options

1. **Option A: Tiered Per-Node Routing (`gemini-3.8-flash` default + `gemini-pro` escalation for high-complexity nodes)**
2. **Option B: Single Frontier Model Everywhere (`gemini-pro` 100%)**
3. **Option C: Single Fast Model Everywhere (`gemini-3.8-flash` 100%)**

## Decision Outcome

**Chosen Option: Option A — Tiered Per-Node Model Routing.**

Each blueprint assigns models per node based on reasoning complexity, risk profile, and latency budget:

| Blueprint & Node | Primary Model | Escalation Model | Traffic Split | Routing Trigger |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **BP01: L1 Triage & Grounded RAG** | `gemini-3.8-flash` | `gemini-pro` | **85% Flash / 15% Pro** | Complexity classifier >= 0.70, multi-system incident, or L1 confidence < 0.80 |
| **BP02: Contract Clause Extraction** | `gemini-3.8-flash` | `gemini-pro` | **75% Flash / 25% Pro** | Clause taxonomy tag in `{INDEMNITY, LIABILITY_CAP, IP_OWNERSHIP, CHANGE_OF_CONTROL, NON_COMPETE}` |
| **BP03: Text-to-SQL & Narrative** | `gemini-3.8-flash` | `gemini-pro` | **70% Flash / 30% Pro** | Schema join count >= 3, window functions / YoY cohort math, or self-correction retry |

## Quantitative Trade-off Matrix (Pricing & Latency Baseline)

| Metric | `gemini-3.8-flash` | `gemini-pro` | Cost Ratio (Pro / Flash) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Input Price (per 1M tokens)** | **$0.15** | $1.25 | **8.33x** |
| **Output Price (per 1M tokens)** | **$0.60** | $5.00 | **8.33x** |
| **Time-to-First-Token (TTFT P50)** | **~280 ms** | ~850 ms | 3.0x slower |
| **Throughput (tokens/sec)** | **~145 tok/s** | ~65 tok/s | 2.2x slower |

### Enterprise Monthly LLM Spend Comparison Across All 3 Blueprints

| Blueprint (Enterprise Tier) | 100% Flash | **Tiered Routing (Chosen)** | 100% Pro | Savings vs 100% Pro |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **BP01: Support (1M req/mo)** | $630.00 | **$1,323.00** (85/15) | $5,250.00 | **-$3,927.00 / mo (-74.8%)** |
| **BP02: Contracts (50k docs/mo)** | $180.00 | **$576.00** (75/25) | $1,500.00 | **-$924.00 / mo (-61.6%)** |
| **BP03: SQL Agent (250k queries/mo)** | $221.25 | **$708.01** (70/30) | $1,843.75 | **-$1,135.74 / mo (-61.6%)** |
| **Combined Enterprise Portfolio** | $1,031.25 | **$2,607.01** | $8,593.75 | **-$5,986.74 / mo (-69.7%)** |

*(Note: For ultra-high-volume pure binary classification or intent tagging nodes exceeding 10M req/mo, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` can be inserted as a Tier-0 pre-filter before `gemini-3.8-flash`.)*

## Consequences

- **Positive**: Saves **$5,986.74/month (-69.7%)** at Enterprise scale while preserving frontier accuracy on high-liability legal clauses and complex multi-join SQL queries.
- **Negative**: Requires maintaining prompt templates and golden evaluation sets across two model checkpoints; routing drift must be monitored in BigQuery (`pro_escalation_share` alert).

## Revisit Triggers

1. Re-evaluate routing ratios quarterly whenever Google Cloud releases new Gemini Flash generations whose benchmark accuracy on internal golden sets closes within 1% of Pro on legal/SQL rubrics.
2. Trigger immediate alert if `pro_escalation_share` drifts > +5% above target for 48 consecutive hours.

adrs.summary: Enterprise support tickets (BP01), M&A/commercial contracts (BP02), and free-text SQL comment columns (BP03) routinely contain regulated PII and financial identifiers (`CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER`, `US_SOCIAL_SECURITY_NUMBER`, `IBAN_CODE`, `EMAIL_ADDRESS`, `PHONE_NUMBER`, `PERSON_NAME`, `IP_ADDRESS`). Sending raw unredacted data directly to LLM prompts or observability logs violates GDPR data minimization, PCI-DSS scope reduction, and enterprise SOC 2 policies.
adrs.decisionOutcome: **Chosen Option: Option A — Managed Cloud DLP with Workload-Specific De-Identification Modes.**
adrs.content:
# ADR-004: Cloud DLP Sensitive Data Anonymization Before Vertex AI Inference

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Date**: 2026-11-23
- **Applies To**: Blueprint 01 (Support), Blueprint 02 (Contracts), Blueprint 03 (SQL Analytics)

## Context

Enterprise support tickets (BP01), M&A/commercial contracts (BP02), and free-text SQL comment columns (BP03) routinely contain regulated PII and financial identifiers (`CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER`, `US_SOCIAL_SECURITY_NUMBER`, `IBAN_CODE`, `EMAIL_ADDRESS`, `PHONE_NUMBER`, `PERSON_NAME`, `IP_ADDRESS`). Sending raw unredacted data directly to LLM prompts or observability logs violates GDPR data minimization, PCI-DSS scope reduction, and enterprise SOC 2 policies.

## Decision Drivers

1. **Zero Raw PII in Prompts or Logs**: Sensitive identifiers must be removed or tokenized *before* Vertex AI inference and *before* Cloud Logging ingestion.
2. **Coreference Preservation for Long Legal Contracts**: Naive masking (`[REDACTED]` everywhere) breaks multi-page legal reasoning in Blueprint 02 when the model must track whether Party A or Party B bears indemnification liability.
3. **Low Latency for Real-Time Chat/Analytics**: Inline PII redaction in Blueprint 01 and Blueprint 03 must add < 120 ms P95 latency.
4. **Fail-Closed Safety**: Privacy controls must never silently fail open during API degradation.

## Considered Options

1. **Option A: Cloud DLP (Sensitive Data Protection) — Inline Masking/Surrogates for Real-Time (BP01/BP03) + Deterministic KMS-Wrapped Tokenization (`CRYPTO_DETERMINISTIC`) for Contracts (BP02)**
2. **Option B: In-House Regex / Presidio Microservice on Cloud Run**
3. **Option C: Post-Hoc Asynchronous DLP Auditing Only (No Pre-LLM Gate)**

## Decision Outcome

**Chosen Option: Option A — Managed Cloud DLP with Workload-Specific De-Identification Modes.**

- **Blueprint 01 (Support) & Blueprint 03 (SQL Output)**: Synchronous `projects.content.deidentify` using `REPLACE_WITH_INFO_TYPE` / ephemeral surrogate tokens (`[EMAIL_1]`, `[CARD_1]`) for fast < 90 ms P95 redaction.
- **Blueprint 02 (Contracts)**: Cloud Workflows invokes `projects.content.deidentify` with `CRYPTO_DETERMINISTIC` (AES-SIV wrapped by **Cloud KMS CMEK**), producing stable per-entity tokens across 20–150 pages so Gemini Pro preserves party coreference while remaining 100% blind to real identities.

## Quantitative Trade-off Matrix

| Criterion | Cloud DLP (Managed) | Self-Hosted Presidio / Regex | Async Post-Hoc Only |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Built-in Global InfoTypes** | **150+ maintained InfoTypes** (Luhn/checksum + ML context) | ~30 basic recognizers (high maintenance) | 150+ (too late) |
| **Cost (BP01 Growth: 100k req/mo, 0.4 GB)** | **$1.20 / mo** ($3.00/GB inspect+deid) | ~$45 / mo (always-on NLP container RAM) | $0.40 / mo |
| **Cost (BP02 Growth: 5k contracts/mo, 0.3 GB)** | **$0.90 / mo** | ~$65 / mo | $0.30 / mo |
| **P95 Latency Overhead** | **65 – 110 ms** (regional endpoint) | 180 – 450 ms (spaCy NER CPU) | 0 ms (unsafe) |
| **Prevents PII Reaching LLM** | **Yes (100% fail-closed gate)** | Partial (lower recall on international IDs) | **No (Compliance Failure)** |
| **Deterministic Coreference (KMS)** | **Native (`CRYPTO_DETERMINISTIC`)** | Custom crypto engineering required | N/A |

## Consequences

- **Positive**: Negligible cost ($0.09–$15.00/mo across all tiers); eliminates custom NER model maintenance; enforces structural privacy separation in BP02 (`sa-contract-worker` has IAM access only to post-DLP tokenized storage).
- **Negative**: Adds ~80 ms latency to synchronous paths; requires careful InfoType likelihood tuning (`LIKELY` vs `POSSIBLE`) to avoid over-redacting benign technical terms (e.g., error codes mistaken for phone numbers).

## Revisit Triggers

1. Revisit if raw inspected payload volume exceeds **50 TB/month** ($150k/mo DLP spend), where a hybrid local pre-filter + Cloud DLP selective scan becomes cost-optimal.
2. Tune custom InfoType exclusion dictionaries whenever false-positive redaction rate exceeds 1.5% on weekly BigQuery QA audits.

# ADR-005: Zero-Trust Private IAM OIDC, Vercel BFF Pattern & VPC-SC Isolation

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Date**: 2026-11-23
- **Applies To**: Blueprint 01 (Support), Blueprint 02 (Contracts), Blueprint 03 (SQL Analytics)

## Context

Exposing AI agent APIs, RAG retrievers, or MCP SQL servers as public `--allow-unauthenticated` Cloud Run endpoints with static API keys creates severe risks: credential leakage in client bundles, lateral movement across microservices, and data exfiltration from Cloud Storage, Firestore, or BigQuery. At the same time, modern enterprise web portals (often hosted on **Vercel** or **Cloud Run**) need a clean, low-latency way to authenticate to private GCP backends without embedding long-lived Service Account JSON keys.

## Decision Drivers

1. **Zero Public Internal Services**: Internal microservices (`sa-rag-reader`, `sa-support-agent`, `sa-mcp-sql-ro`, `sa-clm-notifier`) must reject all unauthenticated and non-VPC traffic.
2. **Zero Static Service Account Keys**: Enforce GCP Org Policy `constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation` across production projects.
3. **Defense Against Data Exfiltration**: Even if an IAM token is compromised, exfiltrating GCS buckets, Firestore collections, or BigQuery datasets outside the enterprise perimeter must be blocked at the control plane.
4. **End-User Identity Propagation**: Downstream services (especially Blueprint 03 SQL RLS) must trust only cryptographically verified user claims.

## Considered Options

1. **Option A: Private IAM OIDC + IAP/Vercel BFF (Workload Identity Federation) + Private Service Connect (PSC) + VPC Service Controls (VPC-SC)**
2. **Option B: Static API Keys + Public Cloud Run Endpoints + App-Level Bearer Tokens**
3. **Option C: Full Istio Service Mesh on GKE with mTLS Everywhere**

## Decision Outcome

**Chosen Option: Option A — Zero-Trust Private IAM OIDC, BFF Pattern, PSC, and VPC-SC.**

- **Service-to-Service Auth**: Every internal Cloud Run service sets `ingress = internal` and grants `roles/run.invoker` exclusively to its specific upstream Service Account using Google-signed **OIDC ID tokens** (auto-rotated hourly via GCE Metadata Server).
- **Frontend / Edge Auth (Vercel BFF or IAP)**:
  - For internal portals (BP03), **Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)** terminates corporate SSO and injects cryptographically signed `X-Goog-IAP-JWT-Assertion` headers.
  - For external customer web apps hosted on **Vercel**, Next.js Route Handlers act as a **Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)** exchanging Vercel OIDC tokens via **GCP Workload Identity Federation (WIF)** for short-lived GCP OIDC tokens — zero static JSON keys stored in Vercel env vars.
- **Network & Perimeter**: All Google APIs (Vertex AI, Firestore, BigQuery, Document AI, Cloud DLP, Cloud SQL) are reached over **Private Service Connect (PSC)** inside a **VPC Service Controls (VPC-SC)** perimeter. Outbound SaaS traffic (Zendesk, Jira, CLM) exits strictly through **Direct VPC Egress + Cloud NAT** with static allowlisted IPs.

## Quantitative Trade-off Matrix

| Criterion | Private IAM OIDC + PSC + VPC-SC | Public Cloud Run + Static API Keys | GKE + Istio mTLS Mesh |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Static Credential Exposure Risk** | **Zero** (short-lived OIDC / WIF tokens) | High (key sprawl & rotation drift) | Low |
| **Exfiltration Protection (Stolen Token)** | **Blocked by VPC-SC perimeter** | None | Network-only (no GCP API perimeter) |
| **Monthly Control Plane Cost** | **$7.30/mo** (PSC) + **$0** (IAM/IAP/VPC-SC) | $0 / mo | ~$350+/mo (GKE + mesh overhead) |
| **Implementation Complexity** | Medium (Terraform modules) | Low (insecure) | Very High |
| **Auditability** | Native Cloud Audit Logs per SA & IAP user | Weak (shared static key) | High (requires custom telemetry) |

## Consequences

- **Positive**: Eliminates entire classes of credential-theft and exfiltration attacks; zero static SA keys; $0 licensing cost for IAM, IAP, and VPC-SC.
- **Negative**: Requires upfront VPC-SC dry-run validation (recommended 14 days in dry-run mode before enforcing) to avoid breaking CI/CD pipelines or developer tooling.

## Revisit Triggers

1. Audit VPC-SC ingress/egress rules whenever adding a new SaaS integration or cross-project BigQuery Analytics Hub share.
2. Enable **Binary Authorization** on Cloud Run if regulatory scope expands to FedRAMP High or PCI-DSS Level 1.

# ADR-006: Standardizing Tool Access via MCP and Agent Delegation via A2A

- **Status**: Accepted
- **Date**: 2026-11-23
- **Applies To**: Blueprint 03 (Production MCP Read-Only SQL Server) & Optional Extension Pattern for Blueprint 01 (Cross-Agent A2A Delegation & Ticketing MCP)

## Context

As enterprises deploy multiple specialized AI agents (Technical Support in BP01, Contract Risk in BP02, SQL Analytics in BP03), hardcoding database clients, Zendesk/Jira REST wrappers, and inter-agent HTTP glue directly inside each agent's prompt loop creates **N × M integration sprawl**, duplicated security logic (SQL AST validation, DLP scrubbing, rate limiting), and tight coupling to a single LLM framework.

## Decision Drivers

1. **Deterministic Security Boundary**: Tool execution (SQL queries, ticket creation) must run in an isolated process with independent IAM credentials and deterministic guardrails — completely separated from the LLM orchestration runtime.
2. **Protocol Interoperability**: Tools built once (e.g., the read-only BigQuery/Cloud SQL server in BP03) should be consumable by ADK agents, IDE copilots, and future agent frameworks without rewriting adapters.
3. **Multi-Agent Composition**: Support agents (BP01) may need to delegate billing/usage lookups to the Analytics Agent (BP03) without merging their IAM scopes or codebases.

## Considered Options

1. **Option A: Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Tool Servers + Agent2Agent (A2A) for Cross-Agent Delegation**
2. **Option B: Monolithic Agent with In-Process Python Tool Functions**
3. **Option C: Custom Proprietary REST/gRPC Microservices per Agent**

## Decision Outcome

**Chosen Option: Option A — MCP for Deterministic Tool Boundaries + A2A for Inter-Agent Delegation.**

- **MCP (Vertical Agent-to-Tool Boundary)**: Every privileged external/data capability (e.g., `execute_readonly_sql` and `get_authorized_schema` in BP03; `create_support_ticket` in BP01) is exposed as a stateless **MCP Streamable HTTP** server on private Cloud Run v2 with its own least-privilege Service Account (`sa-mcp-sql-ro`).
- **A2A (Horizontal Agent-to-Agent Boundary)**: When one domain agent delegates a multi-turn task to another domain agent (e.g., Support Agent requesting an account usage summary from SQL Analytics Agent), agents communicate via **A2A Agent Cards (`/.well-known/agent.json`)** over private Cloud Run OIDC IAM — preserving strict domain IAM isolation.

## Quantitative Trade-off Matrix

| Criterion | MCP + A2A on Cloud Run | In-Process Monolithic Tools | Custom REST Glue |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **IAM Blast Radius Isolation** | **Strict** (separate SA per MCP server) | **None** (LLM runtime holds DB/API creds) | Strict (high boilerplate) |
| **Integration Complexity (N agents × M tools)** | **O(N + M)** (standardized schemas) | O(N × M) duplicated code | O(N × M) custom clients |
| **Added Network Hop Latency** | **+8 – 18 ms** (same-region private Cloud Run) | 0 ms | +8 – 18 ms |
| **Cross-Framework Reuse (ADK, Claude, IDEs)** | **Native** (standard MCP JSON-RPC) | Zero | Requires custom SDK per client |
| **Centralized Audit & Guardrail Enforcement** | **100%** (AST, RLS, DLP in one MCP node) | Fragmented across agent repos | Fragmented |

## Consequences

- **Positive**: Eliminates DB credential exposure in LLM containers; enables 100% reuse of the guarded SQL MCP server across internal teams; clean A2A contract boundaries for multi-agent enterprise scale.
- **Negative**: Adds ~12 ms internal network hop and requires propagating verified end-user IAP/OIDC identity claims in signed headers from agent to MCP server.

## Revisit Triggers

1. Re-evaluate A2A transport bindings if high-frequency (< 50 ms) streaming agent-to-agent coordination requires gRPC bidirectional streaming over Cloud Run HTTP/2.
2. Enforce centralized **MCP Server Registry & Schema Approval** in CI/CD once the organization exceeds 10 production MCP servers.
